topic: Gravity and Its Effects on Objects
key_concepts: Gravity is a non-contact attractive force between any two objects.
Gravity pulls objects toward the center of the Earth.
Gravity's strength depends on the masses of the objects.
Gravity's strength depends on the distance between objects.
Sir Isaac Newton discovered gravity after observing a falling apple.
The word gravity comes from the Latin word gravitas, meaning weight.
Without air resistance, heavy and light objects fall at the same rate.
Gravity keeps objects and people grounded on Earth.
Gravity causes unsupported objects to fall.
Gravity causes ocean tides and keeps planets in orbit around the Sun.
Free-fall is motion under the influence of gravity only.
Air resistance affects the motion of falling objects.
